testimonials.name: Arjun Pradeep
testimonials.highlight_quote: During the process of activating the Maha Theerthas and the three Shiva Lingams, I could actually feel subtle sensations in my body... On the last day's meditation, I felt something really special during the Shiva Mandala and the merging process.
testimonials.full_testimonial:
The Beyond the Mind retreat was a really positive experience. Since this was my second time attending, it felt even more special doing it at Kanyakumari.

We started the first day with Pooja Veppu for ourselves, which was a great way to begin.

During the process of activating the Maha Theerthas and the three Shiva Lingams, I could actually feel subtle sensations in my body.

On the last day's meditation, even though there were many mandalas, I felt something really special during the Shiva Mandala and the merging process.

Learning about entity removal and getting to know about our spirit guides was very insightful. The soul liberation process was also a very good and experiential process.

Overall, it gave me a wonderful sense of calm and connection.

Thank you Pradeep Sir and a heartfelt thanks to all who were part of this retreat.

testimonials.name: Community Circle Reflection
testimonials.highlight_quote: Going from chaotic laughter to a quiet room is the hardest part... I'm already counting down the days until we gather again.
testimonials.full_testimonial: A reflection captured on the official BTM 2026 gathering poster, embodying the deep familial kinship, shared tears of release, and warm laughter that naturally blossoms when seekers come together under sincere guidance.

faqs.question: When should I arrive for Beyond the Mind 2027 in Rishikesh?
faqs.answer: Participants should arrive on Tuesday, October 5, 2027 by 2:45 PM for sanctuary check-in, room settlement, orientation, and gentle acclimatization by the Ganges. The intensive retreat sessions run across four full days from Wednesday, October 6 to Saturday, October 9, 2027.

faqs.question: What language will the retreat sessions be conducted in?
faqs.answer: The retreat sessions will be conducted in English, with Hindi translation available for participants who require it. This ensures all participants experience complete clarity and depth throughout every session.

faqs.question: What are the modes of participation available for the retreat?
faqs.answer: The Divine Retreat is available in both offline (in-person at our Rishikesh sanctuary) and online live streaming formats. Whether joining us physically on the banks of Ganga or tuning in from home, participants receive direct guided instructions and energy attunements.

faqs.question: What is Daily Guided Meditation and how do I join?
faqs.answer: Daily Guided Meditation is an ongoing regular activity of Beyond the Mind. Held online via Zoom Monday to Friday at 7:30 PM IST, these paid sessions offer an opportunity to pause, observe, and transcend daily mental noise. You can enquire anytime via our WhatsApp concierge or online form.

faqs.question: What will the weather be like in Rishikesh in October, and what clothes are required?
faqs.answer: October in Rishikesh offers idyllic post-monsoon autumn weather. Daytime temperatures are pleasantly warm (28°C–30°C / 82°F–86°F) under clear blue skies, while nights and early mornings cool down to a crisp 15°C–18°C (59°F–64°F). Bring comfortable, loose cotton/linen clothing for meditation (modest attire covering shoulders and knees), plus a light shawl, stole, or cardigan for early morning sessions and evening Ganga Aarti, along with slip-on sandals.

faqs.question: Can I explore Rishikesh attractions like Bungee Jumping and River Rafting?
faqs.answer: Yes! Rishikesh offers iconic adventures including India's highest 83m Bungee Jumping (Jumpin Heights at Mohan Chatti), white water river rafting on Ganga rapids, visiting the Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia), meditation at Vashistha Cave, trekking to Neer Garh waterfalls, and the timeless evening Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat.

faqs.question: How do I register for the retreat?
faqs.answer: You can submit your registration through our demo registration card on the website or connect directly with our coordinators on WhatsApp. Once your registration is received, our team personally confirms availability and shares payment options.

faqs.question: What are the accommodation and meal arrangements?
faqs.answer: We offer private single occupancy, twin sharing, and non-residential options. Pure, wholesome sattvic vegetarian meals and Ayurvedic teas are prepared fresh daily to support energetic clarity and meditative depth.

faqs.question: Who is guiding the retreat and meditation sessions?
faqs.answer: The retreat and daily meditation are guided by Pradeep Sir under the spiritual vision of Beyond the Mind and Moola Brahman, emphasizing authentic experiential stillness without dogmatic constraints.

attractions.title: India's Highest Bungee Jumping (83m)
attractions.description: Located at Mohan Chatti, experience India's first and highest fixed-platform bungee jumping with international jump masters from New Zealand. Leap into the misty river valley for an exhilarating surge of courage.
highlights: 83-meter jump platform
Trained by New Zealand safety experts
Includes Extreme Flying Fox & Giant Swing options

attractions.title: White Water River Rafting on Ganga
attractions.description: Navigate world-renowned Grade III and IV rapids (such as The Wall, Roller Coaster, Three Blind Mice, and Golf Course) amidst breathtaking Himalayan river canyon landscapes.
highlights: Options from Marine Drive (24km) or Shivpuri (16km)
Certified river guides & safety gear
Cliff jumping and body surfing included

attractions.title: Sacred Evening Ganga Aarti at Triveni Ghat
attractions.description: Witness the mesmerizing ritual of thousands of oil lamps, conch shells blowing, and Sanskrit hymns echoing across the holy river as priests perform the evening Vedic offering.
highlights: Floating diya offerings on the river
Ancient Vedic chanting and brass lamp choreography
Parmarth Niketan & Triveni Ghat ceremonies

attractions.title: The Beatles Ashram (Chaurasi Kutia)
attractions.description: The historic Maharishi Mahesh Yogi ashram where The Beatles stayed in 1968 to study Transcendental Meditation. Features 84 meditation stone igloos, murals, and vibrant jungle tranquility.
highlights: 84 meditation stone meditation caves
Beatles cathedral graffiti & photo gallery
Scenic forest overlook inside Rajaji Tiger Reserve boundary

attractions.title: Vashistha Gufa (Ancient Silent Meditation Cave)
attractions.description: An ancient natural cave directly on the banks of Ganga where Sage Vashistha meditated. The deep silence inside is legendary for spontaneous meditative absorption and inner quiet.
highlights: Natural rock cave with deep silent vibrations
Shivling consecrated within the cave
Private white sand riverbank right outside the cave
attractions.location_tip: Badrinath Road (25 km upstream of Rishikesh)

attractions.title: Neer Garh & Patna Waterfalls Trek
attractions.description: A refreshing hike through dense Himalayan forest canopy leading to tiered jade-green natural plunge pools and cascading mountain waterfalls.
highlights: Natural limestone spring water pools
Gentle hike through Garhwal flora and fauna
Rustic tea stalls along mountain trails
attractions.location_tip: Neer Garh (approx. 5 km from Lakshman Jhula)

weatherClothing.summary: October is widely celebrated as the finest month to visit Rishikesh. The monsoon has passed, leaving crystalline Himalayan skies, crystal emerald river currents, and clean mountain air. Days are sunny and comfortably warm, while early mornings and evenings bring a crisp, refreshing mountain breeze.
clothing_tips: Meditation Attire: Loose, breathable cotton or linen clothing allowing easy floor sitting, cross-legged postures, and diaphragmatic breathing.
Morning & Evening Layering: A light woolen shawl, stole, pashmina, or light cardigan for cool riverside meditations and evening Ganga Aarti.
Temple & Ashram Modesty: Rishikesh is a revered pilgrimage sanctuary. Modest clothing covering shoulders and knees is required at temples and spiritual halls.
Footwear: Easy slip-on sandals or walking shoes that can be quickly slipped off before entering meditation spaces and riverbanks.
Sun & Hydration: Sunglasses, natural sun protection, and a refillable stainless steel water bottle.
recommended_items: 2-3 sets of white or earth-tone comfortable meditation pants/kurtas
Light shawl or cardigan for mornings/evenings (15°C–18°C)
Personal notebook or journal for reflections
